display_name: Local Ollama vision model (qwen3-vl 4B, VLM perception)

metadata.thinking_note: extra_body EXISTS TO TURN THINKING OFF. qwen3-vl reasons before answering, and the reasoning is billed against max_tokens: at 1024 AND at 3072 it returned finish_reason=length with an EMPTY message.content (10275 chars of reasoning, no JSON). The reasoning proved the model READS the board correctly - it named the player and the top card - so this is purely an output-budget problem. Prompt wording ('/no_think') did not help; only a server-side flag does. Both spellings are sent because the name differs per runtime (Ollama: think, HF chat template: chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking) and unknown JSON fields are ignored by these servers. If reasoning_chars is still large in provider_empty_content after this, the build honours NEITHER flag - switch model_name to a non-thinking VLM (qwen2.5vl, minicpm-v, llava) rather than raising the budget again.
metadata.setup: Pick a VLM whose architecture your Ollama build supports: ollama show <model> must list 'vision' under Capabilities AND the model must actually load. Ollama serves an OpenAI-compatible API at :11434/v1
metadata.arch_warning: DO NOT use llama3.2-vision here. Its architecture is 'mllama', which Ollama 0.32.5 cannot load at all: a plain TEXT request returns 500 with 'llama-server process has terminated: exit status 1: error loading model: unknown model architecture: mllama'. It failed on every perception call. qwen3vl IS supported on this build (verified with aeline/opan and qwen3-vl-5-4b).
metadata.timeout_note: timeout_seconds must stay BELOW VLM_TIMEOUT_S (.env, 180) which must stay below VLM_HTTP_TIMEOUT_SEC (280); innermost budget fails first so the error names the real cause instead of a ReadTimeout further out
metadata.model_choice: Avoid a tiny 'thinking' VLM (aeline/opan, qwen3vl 2.1B): a 2B model cannot read fanned, rotated, glossy card glyphs, and reasoning tokens compete with the JSON for the token budget.
metadata.json_mode_note: supports_json_mode is deliberately FALSE. It makes providers.py send response_format={type:json_object}, which Ollama maps to format=json - an extra failure surface we do not need, since _parse_structured() already extracts the JSON substring between the first { and the last } from plain text. Re-enable only after verifying the exact model handles it.
